Oregon is 295 miles (475 km) north to south at longest distance, and 395 miles (636 km) east to west. It is the ninth largest state in the U.S.[[70]](#cite_note-72) Oregon's highest point is the summit of [Mount Hood](/wiki/Mount_Hood "Mount Hood"), at 11,249 feet (3,429 m), and its lowest point is the sea level of the Pacific Ocean along the Oregon Coast.[[71]](#cite_note-usgs-73) Oregon's mean elevation is 3,300 feet (1,006 m). [Crater Lake National Park](/wiki/Crater_Lake_National_Park "Crater Lake National Park"), the state's only national park, is the site of the deepest lake in the U.S. at 1,943 feet (592 m).[[72]](#cite_note-74) Oregon claims the [D River](/wiki/D_River "D River") as the shortest river in the world,[[73]](#cite_note-driver-75) though the state of Montana makes the same claim of its [Roe River](/wiki/Roe_River "Roe River").[[74]](#cite_note-roeriver-76)

The acronym *FANG* was coined in 2013 by [Jim Cramer](/wiki/Jim_Cramer "Jim Cramer"), to refer to [Facebook](/wiki/Meta_Platforms "Meta Platforms"), [Amazon](/wiki/Amazon_(company) "Amazon (company)"), [Netflix](/wiki/Netflix,_Inc "Netflix, Inc"), and [Google](/wiki/Alphabet_Inc. "Alphabet Inc."). Cramer called these companies "totally dominant in their markets."[[74]](#cite_note-cnbc_cramer_2013-74) Cramer stated that the four companies were poised to "take a bite out of" the declining market, giving a double meaning to the acronym, according to Cramer's colleague at RealMoney.com, Bob Lang.[[74]](#cite_note-cnbc_cramer_2013-74)[[75]](#cite_note-75)[[76]](#cite_note-fool-76) Cramer expanded FANG to FAANG in 2017, adding [Apple](/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") to the list because its revenue made it a potential [*Fortune* 500](/wiki/Fortune_500 "Fortune 500") company.[[77]](#cite_note-77)

Following Facebook's name change to Meta Platforms in October 2021, as well as the 2015 creation of Google [holding company](/wiki/Holding_company "Holding company") Alphabet, Cramer suggested replacing FAANG with MAMAA, replacing Netflix with [Microsoft](/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") because Netflix's valuation had fallen behind the other companies. With Microsoft, these companies were each valued at over $900 billion compared to Netflix's $310 billion.[[73]](#cite_note-cnbc_mamaa-73) In November 2021, [The Motley Fool](/wiki/The_Motley_Fool "The Motley Fool") suggested MANAMANA (a reference to the 1968 song "[Mah Nà Mah Nà](/wiki/Mah_N%C3%A0_Mah_N%C3%A0 "Mah Nà Mah Nà")") as an acronym that stands for Microsoft, Apple, Netflix, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, [Nvidia](/wiki/Nvidia "Nvidia"), and [Adobe](/wiki/Adobe_Inc. "Adobe Inc.").[[78]](#cite_note-78)

Greenland :: part 04 :: chunk_0003
**Greenland**[[d]](#cite_note-18) is an [autonomous territory](/wiki/Autonomous_administrative_division "Autonomous administrative division")[[e]](#cite_note-21) of the [Kingdom of Denmark](/wiki/Danish_Realm "Danish Realm")[[17]](#cite_note-22)[[18]](#cite_note-23) and is the largest of the kingdom's three constituent parts by land area, the others being [Denmark](/wiki/Denmark "Denmark") proper and the [Faroe Islands](/wiki/Faroe_Islands "Faroe Islands"). Citizens of Greenland are [citizens of Denmark](/wiki/Danish_nationality_law "Danish nationality law"). They are thus [citizens of the European Union](/wiki/European_Union_citizenship "European Union citizenship") (EU), although Greenland is [not part of the EU](/wiki/Special_territories_of_members_of_the_European_Economic_Area#Overseas_countries_and_territories "Special territories of members of the European Economic Area"). It is the [world's largest island](/wiki/List_of_islands_by_area "List of islands by area")[[f]](#cite_note-25) and lies between the [Arctic](/wiki/Arctic_Ocean "Arctic Ocean") and Atlantic oceans, east of the Canadian [Arctic Archipelago](/wiki/Arctic_Archipelago "Arctic Archipelago"). It shares a small 1.2-kilometre (0.75 mi) border with Canada on [Hans Island](/wiki/Hans_Island "Hans Island"). The capital and largest city is [Nuuk](/wiki/Nuuk "Nuuk").[[20]](#cite_note-worldfactbook-26) [Kaffeklubben Island](/wiki/Kaffeklubben_Island "Kaffeklubben Island") off the northern coast is the world's [northernmost undisputed point of land](/wiki/Northernmost_point_of_land "Northernmost point of land")[[g]](#cite_note-27) – [Cape Morris Jesup](/wiki/Cape_Morris_Jesup "Cape Morris Jesup") on the main island was thought to be so until the 1960s. Economically, Greenland is heavily reliant on [aid from Denmark](/wiki/Block_grant#Denmark "Block grant"), which has averaged 5.4 billion [kr.](/wiki/Danish_krone "Danish krone") ([€](/wiki/Euro "Euro")724 million) annually

fanoutqa_038170.x:
Nick Nurse :: Coaching career :: Philadelphia 76ers (2023–present) :: chunk_0007
On June 1, 2023, the [Philadelphia 76ers](/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") announced that Nurse had been hired as their head coach.[[37]](#cite_note-37) His experience game-planning defensively against their reigning MVP center [Joel Embiid](/wiki/Joel_Embiid "Joel Embiid") in the past was considered helpful perspective, namely to help strategize for Embiid to succeed in playoff situations.[[38]](#cite_note-38)[[39]](#cite_note-39)

During the [2023–24 season](/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Philadelphia_76ers_season "2023–24 Philadelphia 76ers season"), Nurse and the 76ers topped the Raptors 114–107 in his return to Toronto as an opposing coach on October 28.[[40]](#cite_note-40) Despite injuries to Embiid and other players throughout the season, Nurse was able to secure a 47–35 record and a play-in tournament victory for the Sixers against the No. 8 seed Heat. As the No. 7 seed, they were eliminated in six games by the [New York Knicks](/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") in the first round of the [playoffs](/wiki/2024_NBA_playoffs "2024 NBA playoffs").[[41]](#cite_note-41)

The [2024–25 season](/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Philadelphia_76ers_season "2024–25 Philadelphia 76ers season") ended in a 24–58 record, the 76ers' first time missing the playoffs since 2017.[[42]](#cite_note-42)

The island of Hokkaido is located in the north of Japan, near [Russia](/wiki/Russia "Russia") ([Sakhalin Oblast](/wiki/Sakhalin_Oblast "Sakhalin Oblast")). It has coastlines on the [Sea of Japan](/wiki/Sea_of_Japan "Sea of Japan") (to the west of the island), the [Sea of Okhotsk](/wiki/Sea_of_Okhotsk "Sea of Okhotsk") (to the north), and the [Pacific Ocean](/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") (to the east). The center of the island is mountainous, with [volcanic plateaux](/wiki/Volcanic_plateau "Volcanic plateau"). Hokkaido has multiple plains such as the [Ishikari Plain](/wiki/Ishikari_Plain "Ishikari Plain") 3,800 km2 (1,500 mi2), [Tokachi Plain](/wiki/Tokachi_Plain "Tokachi Plain") 3,600 km2 (1,400 mi2), the [Kushiro Plain](/w/index.php?title=Kushiro_Plain&action=edit&redlink=1 "Kushiro Plain (page does not exist)") 2,510 km2

Further information: [List of California wildfires](/wiki/List_of_California_wildfires "List of California wildfires")

The timing of "fire season" in California is variable, depending on the amount of prior winter and spring precipitation, the frequency and severity of weather such as heat waves and wind events, and moisture content in vegetation. [Northern California](/wiki/Northern_California "Northern California") typically sees wildfire activity between late spring and early fall, peaking in the summer with hotter and drier conditions. Occasional cold frontal passages can bring wind and lightning. The timing of fire season in Southern California is similar, peaking between late spring and fall. The severity and duration of peak activity in either part of the state is modulated in part by weather events: downslope/offshore wind events can lead to critical fire weather, while onshore flow and Pacific weather systems can bring conditions that hamper wildfire growth.[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[5]](#cite_note-:02-5)
